headline: Dragulescu-Yakovenko 2000 (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; stationary P(m) exponential (loglin R^2=1.000, fitted T=100.1 vs <m>=100); Gini=0.500, CV=1.000 (exponential fixed point); money conserved to |dM|/M=4.7e-16

verdicts.gate: P1 stationary P(m) is exponential (Boltzmann-Gibbs): loglin R^2>=0.95, slope~1/<m>, mode in lowest bin, exp AIC < power-law AIC (not interior-peaked)
P2 inequality at the exponential fixed point: Gini = 0.50+-0.03 AND CV = 1.0+-0.1
P3 money conserved (|dM|/M<1e-9, min money>=0) and fitted T within 10% of <m>

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the universal exponential (Boltzmann-Gibbs) money distribution with Gini=0.5, and would catch a saving-propensity (peaked-Gamma) artifact

citations: Dragulescu, A. & Yakovenko, V.M. (2000). Statistical mechanics of money. European Physical Journal B 17:723-729. doi:10.1007/s100510070114.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the exponential-shape fit, Gini/CV at the fixed point, and money conservation
